headlines.headline: Futures held a firmer tech-led bid into the final premarket hour: Nasdaq 100 futures ~+1% and S&P 500 futures +0.4% (Investopedia, ~8am ET), while Dow futures faded to -0.2% from +0.04% at 5:45am ET (TipRanks). The Roundhill Mag-7 ETF (MAGS) is +0.5% after a -2% Friday; CoreWeave +2% premarket after plunging 25% last week on debt concerns; the Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM) rebounded 4% after -6% Friday.
headlines.why_it_matters: The bounce is broadening across the most beaten-down AI names, but the Dow fade shows it is a tech-led squeeze, not a broad risk-on day - the open has to confirm it before it counts as repaired.

headlines.headline: AI-chip rebound: SMH +2.7% premarket, SOXX +3% after a -4% Friday, NVDA +1.35%, AMD +3.26%, AVGO +2.67%, MU/SNDK/WDC/STX up to +4.5%; Lam Research +4% premarket despite reporting this week (TipRanks, CTT briefing). SOXX has fallen eight straight sessions - first time since 2008 - while Cantor says chip equipment is sold out (CTT).
headlines.why_it_matters: Chips are the engine of this morning's bid - an eight-session washout usually snaps hard, but it only matters if SOXX breaks the losing streak at the open and new lows start shrinking.

headlines.headline: Meta lagged the bounce, -0.26% premarket (TipRanks), with Tesla (-0.37%), Netflix (-0.27%) and IBM (-0.31%) also soft. Reuters says Meta is expected to beat Wall Street estimates when it reports Wednesday AMC, after Friday's -3.72% - the steepest Mag-7 drop.
headlines.why_it_matters: Investors are de-risking into Wednesday's print - Friday's hangover plus earnings caution; capex guidance is what decides whether the AI-supply-chain fear trade resumes or fades.

headlines.headline: Tesla -0.37% premarket ahead of Wednesday's print (TipRanks); SpaceX reports Tuesday night. Musk's pledge of one SpaceX share to every US child (~$10.5B) is circulating in the tape.
headlines.why_it_matters: Same two-day de-risking pattern as Meta - the print plus SpaceX results and merger rumors keep both legs of the Musk complex news-sensitive this week.

headlines.why_it_matters: The CMA probe is long-dated and consultative, so it pressures the returns-on-AI narrative more than near-term cash flow; today MSFT is trading with the tape.

analysis: What changed vs the 5:00am brief: the tech bid held (Nasdaq 100 futures ~+1%) but the Dow faded to -0.2% - a value-to-tech rotation inside the bounce. Memory chips became the bounce's leaders (DRAM ETF +4%, WDC/SNDK/MU/STX up to +4.5%), Lam Research +4% despite reporting this week, and JPMorgan's INTC upgrade plus Truist's $355 NBIS target added hard analyst legs under the beaten-down names. New items: the AEP/X-Energy/Amazon 960MW nuclear study, the TTMI/Ophir $650M deal, EOSE's beat-but-trim guide, and RCAT's Steyr offer (all single-source via the CTT briefing). The flip side: Meta, Tesla, Netflix and IBM are all lagging the premarket bid on earnings caution - a two-speed tape ahead of Wednesday's double print. Internals read like a textbook deeply-oversold bounce (2,102 up vs 1,082 down premarket; only 25% above the 40-day; new lows 164 vs highs 46) - bounces from these levels snap hard, but they only become bottoms when new lows start shrinking. Signal vs noise: the PBOC tool, EU energy stress, and the AI-credit overhang (CRWV CDS >1,000bp, still untouched) are durable threads; the DPRK-missile chatter and single-source deal items are noise until confirmed. The open at 6:30 PT is the first real test.
